subject: Borealis integration: post-call recap + routing & policy next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire@borealis.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Borealis integration: post-call recap + routing & policy next steps

Hi Claire / Luca —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on architecture, auth, and the routing/policy constraints you mentioned. I kept this focused on what we can ship in the pilot (4–6 weeks) vs. what’s longer-term.

Summary of needs you described
- Use case: support-ticket triage + dynamic reranking for knowledge base answers; embed + rerank candidate passages, then run structured tool-calls to fetch customer metadata.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for in-region reads (EU customers).
- Throughput: bursts up to ~300 qps for embed+rerank flows during peak hours.
- Data residency: EU-only for PII paths; non-PII experimental traffic can go to other regions.
- Auth: service-account API keys + mutual TLS for the private control-plane (recommended).

Proposed pilot architecture (high level)
1) SDK & auth
- Recommend JS/Node SDK for backend integration (we’ll provide example middleware for request signing).
- Use per-service account API keys, rotate via your KMS. If you want mTLS we can enable Mutual TLS on the Private control-plane and provide cert guidance.

2) Model routing & policy (pilot defaults)
- Primary model (EU): redwood-xl-8k (fp16) in eu-west-1; route all production user requests here.
- Fallback #1 (EU quantized): redwood-medium-8k-quant (faster single-node path) for overloaded nodes — keeps traffic in-region and reduces cost at tail latency hit (~+15–25ms).
- Fallback #2 (regional-soft): if EU capacity exhausted and you allow cross-region, we can route to eu-neighbor / minimal-cost instance in eu-central with strict tagging so logs/evts show cross-region. We will NOT fallback to US by default to preserve data residency unless you opt-in.
- Cost policy: cap per-request gas by token budget; if expected token count > threshold, auto-switch to a cheaper model variant or return a truncated structured response.

3) Embeddings + reranker flow
- Embeds served by a dedicated embed pool. Use cache + per-customer prefix caching for hot passages.
- Reranker implemented as a two-step: lightweight lexical filter -> embedding nearest neighbors -> model-based re-rank (reranker model pinned per rollout).

4) Structured output & tool-calling
- Use structured output schema (JSON schema) for the tool-calling step; runtime will validate and surface parsing errors in the console.
- We’ll provide a sample tool adapter for your metadata store (REST) and a transactional retry policy (idempotent calls).

Action items / next steps
- From Borealis: share sample traffic profile (qps by endpoint, token distribution) and security contact for SOC2 evidence — target by Tue 26 May.
- From Redwood: we’ll draft a Minimal SOW and a proposed routing policy (I attached the SOW draft). I’ll also add a short snippet for SDK + sample config you can copy/paste.
- Set up a one-hour technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (Jordan) to validate your network posture and mTLS setup — propose Wed 27 May, 10:00 CET. Can you confirm?

If that all looks right I’ll open the Pilot as BR-2026-0047 and loop in pricing.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: +1 (415) 555-0123

----
Attachment: SOW-draft-20260521.pdf (summary SOW draft for pilot + milestones)

From: Claire Zhou <claire@borealis.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Luca Martell <luca@borealis.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Borealis integration: post-call recap + routing & policy next steps

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the clear summary — this matches our notes. A couple quick questions and clarifications before the technical deep-dive:

1) Fallbacks: can you confirm the expected latency penalty for the quantized fallback vs primary (ballpark ms)? Also if capacity is constrained in eu-west, will requests queue or immediately fall back?
2) Cost: can you provide a rough per-1k-token cost delta between the primary and the quantized fallback for budgeting?
3) Data residency: we need to avoid any automatic cross-border fallback for PII-paths. Would be great to see a routing policy snippet that enforces region-only for endpoints marked PI.
4) SOC2: please share the SOC2 summary doc and the security contact to talk to for an evidence request.

We can do Wed 27 May 10:00 CET for the deep-dive — confirming with our infra team now.

Thanks,
Claire
Head of Platform Integrations | Borealis AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire@borealis.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 17:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Borealis integration: post-call recap + routing & policy next steps

Claire —

Answers inline and a small sample routing policy you can try in the sandbox.

1) Latency delta: primary (redwood-xl-8k): median token latency ~8–12ms/token under steady-state; quantized fallback: ~10–16ms/token depending on sequence length. For end-to-end generation 95th P95 difference is typically +20–40ms. We can do stricter measurements in your traffic profile.

2) Cost delta: very rough public estimate: primary ~ $0.26 / 1k tokens; quantized fallback ~ $0.12 / 1k tokens. Exact depends on token mix and batch efficiency — we’ll run an estimator when you share sample payloads.

3) Behavior when constrained: routing policy supports two modes — queue-within-slo (brief queue up to 250ms) or immediate-fallback. For PII-tagged endpoints we recommend queue-within-slo + no cross-region fallback.

4) SOC2: attaching soc2-summary.pdf. Security contact: security-requests@redwood.com (for evidence exchange).

Sample policy (pseudo-config you can paste into the Console sandbox):

# RoutingPolicy: borealis-pilot-eu
primary: { model: "redwood-xl-8k", region: "eu-west-1", max_qps: 200 }
fallbacks: [
  { model: "redwood-medium-8k-quant", region: "eu-west-1", trigger: "max_queue_time>250ms or cpu>85%" },
  { model: "redwood-mini-cost", region: "eu-central-1", trigger: "manual_opt_in && non_pii" }
]
pii_rules: { endpoints: ["/user/profile","/payments"], region_enforcement: "strict", cross_region_fallback: false }
cost_controls: { token_budget_threshold: 1500, auto_downshift: true }

We’ll bring these as editable fields to the deep-dive so we can tune triggers/thresholds.

Jordan will run through network/mTLS details on Wed 27 May. Vanessa — I’ll need you to prepare an outline of pricing options we can offer for a 6-week pilot (usage cap vs committed).

Cheers,
Marcus

----
Attachment: soc2-summary.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Borealis integration: post-call recap + routing & policy next steps

Looping you both in — Claire confirmed the Wed deep-dive and asked for the stricter PII routing policy + cost deltas. She also requested SOC2 evidence and asked that cross-region fallbacks be disabled for PII endpoints.

Quick internal notes:
- Pricing: they’re early-stage but with clear burstiness. Vanessa, can you prepare: 1) a capped pilot plan (90k tokens/month free credits + overage rate) and 2) a committed option with a 3-month term and a light discount? We may be able to offer a pilot discount given potential ARR upside.
- Jordan: please draft the mTLS checklist + the Console steps to pin region-only routing for endpoints; we should show how to annotate endpoints as PII in the sandbox. Also prep expected latency numbers for the EU quantized fallback under 100/200/300 token seeds.
- I’ll own the SOW draft and the HubSpot updates (BR-2026-0047).

I’ll share a calendar invite for Wed 27 May 10:00 CET once Claire confirms.

Thanks,
Marcus
